newsitem.title: USA: DSP Comm. shares rise after calling off Proxim merger.
newsitem.headline: DSP Comm. shares rise after calling off Proxim merger.

text.p: The stock of DSP Communications Inc. rose sharply Friday after the maker of computer chips for the wireless market said it cancelled its previously announced $400 million acquisition of Proxim Inc.
DSP stock rose $2.75 to $40.75 and Proxim fell 12.5 cents to $19.625 on Nasdaq after the two companies announced they had mutually agreed to terminate their planned merger.

Following the unexpected reduction in the share price of both companies after the planned merger was announced last month, the boards of directors of DSP and Proxim determined they should pursue a working partnership outside the context of a merger.

The total merger-related costs and expenses of DSP, estimated at $5 million, of which $3.45 million will be paid to Proxim, will be charged to DSP's general and administrative expenses during the current quarter it said.
Oppenheimer & Co. analyst Lior Bregman said he upgraded DSP to an outperform from a market perform following news that the deal had been cancelled.
The proposed merger was first announced Oct. 29, and the news sent DSP stock down $17 a share.
In a conference call Friday, Proxim Chief Executive Officer David King said, "We moved to terminate it fast so it would not become a distraction. Trends in our business remain very strong."
"I don't believe there will be any out-of-pocket expenses to Proxim shareholders," King said, referring to the DSP arrangement.
"The majority of our fees and expenses will be covered by this amount," King said, referring to the payment by DSP.
